title.narrative: World Bank Youth Opportunities in Liberia

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve access to income generation opportunities for targeted youth and strengthen the government’s capacity to implement its cash transfer program. The project aims to directly benefit at least 15,000 targeted youth (aged 15–35 years) on a nationwide scale in Liberia.

Svenska ambassaden har fått en förfrågan av Världbsbanken att finansiera projektet "Youth Opportunities Project" med 35 miljoner kronor under perioden 2018-2020.
Huvudsyftet med stödet är att förbättra inkomstmöjligheter bland ungdomar i Liberia. Projektet syftar till att nå 15 000 ungdomar i åldrarna 15-35 år. Minst 50 procent av dessa kommer vara flickor och kvinnor.
Insatsen totala budget är 10 miljoner USD, varav Världsbankens egna finansiering är cirka 6,1 miljoner USD.
Projektet har totalt fyra komponenter: Komponent 1: Socialt stöd för att främja arbete och stöd till hushållsföretag för ungdomar i urbana miljöer Komponent 2: Jordbruksarbete och utbildning Komponent 3: Kapacitet -och systemstärkande stöd till kontantöverföringar Komponent 4: Projektimplementering, kapacitetsbyggande och koordinering
Det svenska stödet kommer rikta in sig på komponent 2 som har två delkomponenter såväl som delkomponent 4.B:
Delkomponent 2A: Jordbruksarbete och utbildning: Målet för denna delkomponent är att förse utsatta ungdomar på landsbygden med stöd till förbättrad konsumtion och inkomst genom jordbruksarbete. 10 000 ungdomar på landsbygden i alla 15 län i landet kommer att förses med enklare utbildning, jordbruksverktyg och jordbruksstöd, samt arbetssubventioner för att delta i gemensamt jordbruk där fokus kommer att vara att öka produktiviteten bland baslivsmedel.
Delkomponent 2B: Kapacitets -och systembyggande: Målet för denna delkomponent är att finansiera kapacitets och systembyggande för Liberia Agency for Community Empowerment (LACE) implementering av stöd till hushållsföretag, jordbruksarbete och enklare utbildning. Delkomponent 4B: Projektimplementering och koordinering av Liberia Agency for Community Empowerment (LACE). Målet för denna delkomponent är att stödja aktiviteter relaterade till projekthantering och koordinering. Detta inkluderar personalrelaterade kostnader, utrustning, fordon, bränsle, kontorsutrymme och kommunikationskostnader. Här ingår även projektrelaterade driftskostnader för LACE under implementeringen av stöd till utbildning, hushållsföretag, jordbruksarbete och kapacitets -och systembyggande delkomponenter av projektet.

The World Bank has applied to The Embassy of Sweden for funding of 35 million SEK to carry out the "Youth Opportunities Project" during 2018-2020.
The main objective of the intervention is to improve access to income generation opportunities for targeted youth. The project aims to directly benefit at least 15,000 targeted youth (aged 15–35 years). At least 50 percent of beneficiaries will be female
The intervention’s total budget is 10 million USD, out of which the organisation’s own funding is approximately 6.1 million USD.
The project has four components:
Component 1: Pre-employment Social Support and Household Enterprises for Urban Youth Component 2: Productive Public Works and Life Skills Support Component 3: Capacity and Systems Building for Cash Transfers Component 4: Project Implementation, Capacity Building, and Coordination
The Swedish support will target component 2 which has two subcomponents as well as subcomponent 4.B: Subcomponent 2A Productive Public Works & Life Skills Training: The objective of this subcomponent is to provide vulnerable youth in rural areas with immediate consumption enhancing support through productive public works and life skills training. 10,000 youth in rural communities in all 15 counties will be provided life skills training, basic farming tools and seedings, agricultural support, as well as labor subsidy to engage in communal farming where the focus will be to enhancing the productivity of staple crops. Subcomponent 2B: Capacity and Systems Building: The objective of this subcomponent is to finance capacity and systems building for LACE for the implementation of household enterprise support, productive public works, and life skills training.
Subcomponent 4B: Project Implementation and Coordination by the Liberia Agency for Community Empowerment (LACE). The objective of this subcomponent is to support activities related to project management and coordination. This includes staff related costs, equipment, vehicles, fuel, office space, and communications costs, and gradual project-related operating costs under LACE for the implementation of the household enterprises, life skills training, productive public works, and capacity and systems building subcomponents of the project.

sector.narrative: Social protection and welfare services policy, planning and administration

description.narrative:
Even though the project development objective was to give income and improved livelihood to 15,000 young people, but Swedish support was targeted at 10,000 of the Community Livelihood and Agriculture Support (CLAS) component. In this regard, final evaluation indicates that the program exceeds targets as the YOP enrolled and provided support to 10,722 poor and vulnerable youths living in difficult and hard to reach rural communities across all 15 Counties in Liberia.
Beneficiaries of the CLAS component cultivated over 5,195 hectares of land with various food crops including Cassava, Ground Nut, Plantain, Pineapple, Corn, Rice, Beans, Watermelon, Banana, and Eddoe. The project also supported a batch of 120 youths in 30 rural communities to successfully establish Agro-Processing setups which continued to provide value addition services to youth farming communities up to project activities closure in September 2021.
Activities under this support impacted young vulnerable people in 357 rural communities across Liberia. Each beneficiary received cash grant of up to US$450 over two farming seasons to enable them to meet their basic household needs during the lean season. The labor subsidies were paid out in multiple tranches based on set farming milestones agreed upon by the Project Team. Each beneficiary was guaranteed 20 days of life skills training to allow them to acquire basic soft skills needed to enhance their participation in the farming groups as well as in the labor market. Beneficiaries were also supported with technical information on best farming practices through practical demonstration on farming site.
YOP maintained a functional Grievances Redress System throughout implementation. The system included: i) a digitized system and toll-free number (3344) through which beneficiarie and other people affected by the project could lodge complaints; ii) Community Oversight Committees (CoCs) and County Steering Committees. Since becoming effective in 2016, the Project GRM recorded 163 cases with 57 coming from beneficiaries under the Community Livelihood and Agriculture Support. Up to project closure, a total of 161 cases (constituting 99 percent of cases) received by the grievance system were successfully resolved.
The overall beneficiary satisfaction rating on the project was recorded at 96 percent (with females on the project having a 97 percent satisfaction rate and males having 95 percent).
The Liberia Agency for Community Empowerment (LACE) was supported to build capacity and ensure that existing structures of YOP remained adequate to support the youth throughout project implementation. Required structures included a dedicated Technical Team to manage implementation at the central level, and a group of service providers (Community Facilitators) to support implementation at the county level. LACE also setup and maintained support to community structures such as Community Oversight Committees that provided oversight on implementation of project activities.
Results from the Satisfaction Survey, which was concluded in early Spring of 2021, put the overall beneficiary satisfaction rating on the project at 96 percent (with females on the project having a 97 percent satisfaction rate and males having 95 percent).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
